cases.sentence: «Твое ___ и счастливого пути!» — крикнул он Зверков.
cases.translation: "To your health and a good journey!" he shouted at Zverkov.
cases.explain: Здоровье is used as an exclamatory toast (a naming/subject form), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: От стола до ___ и от печки обратно к столу.
cases.translation: From the table to the stove and back from the stove to the table.
cases.explain: The preposition до ("up to/as far as") governs the genitive case, hence печки.

cases.translation: Back from the stove to the table.
cases.explain: The preposition к ("towards") always governs the dative case, hence столу.

cases.translation: Zverkov offered me his hand affectionately.
cases.explain: Руку is the direct object of the transitive verb подал ("held out/offered"), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Я пил с горя лафит и херес ___.
cases.translation: In my grief I drank claret and sherry by the glassful.
cases.explain: Стаканами expresses the instrumental of measure/manner ("by the glassful"), hence the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Но уж дело было не в ___.
cases.translation: But the matter was no longer about being first.
cases.explain: The preposition в indicating the topic/matter at hand governs the prepositional case, hence первенстве.

reading.ru: Я еще накануне знал, что приеду первый.
reading.question: What did the narrator already know the day before?
options: That Simonov would pay the bill
reading.correct: That he would arrive first
reading.explain: The narrator says Я еще накануне знал, что приеду первый — he already knew the day before that he would arrive first.

reading.ru: После многих расспросов я добился наконец от слуг, что обед заказан к шести часам, а не к пяти.
reading.question: What did the narrator finally learn from the servants?
options: That dinner was ordered for six o'clock, not five
That dinner had already been eaten
That the other guests had cancelled
reading.correct: That dinner was ordered for six o'clock, not five
reading.explain: He learns что обед заказан к шести часам, а не к пяти — the dinner was ordered for six, not five.

reading.ru: Было еще только двадцать пять минут шестого.
reading.question: What time was it at that point in the narrative?
reading.correct: Twenty-five minutes past five
reading.explain: The text states Было еще только двадцать пять минут шестого — it was only twenty-five minutes past five.

reading.ru: К шести часам, кроме горевших ламп, в комнату внесены были свечи.
reading.question: What was brought into the room by six o'clock besides the burning lamps?
reading.correct: Candles
reading.explain: The text says в комнату внесены были свечи — candles were brought into the room.

reading.ru: В соседней комнате обедали на разных столах два каких-то мрачных посетителя, сердитые с виду и молчавшие.
reading.question: Who was dining in the next room, according to this sentence?
options: Two gloomy, silent-looking guests at separate tables
reading.correct: Two gloomy, silent-looking guests at separate tables
reading.explain: The text describes два каких-то мрачных посетителя, сердитые с виду и молчавшие — two gloomy-looking, silent guests.

reading.ru: Обед был с дамами.
reading.question: What kind of dinner party was happening noisily in a distant room?
reading.correct: A dinner with ladies
reading.explain: The text simply notes Обед был с дамами — the dinner (in the loud room) was with ladies present.

reading.ru: Зверков вошел впереди всех, видимо, предводительствуя.
reading.question: How did Zverkov enter when the group finally arrived?
options: He walked in ahead of everyone, clearly leading them
He arrived alone, before the others
He sent a servant in first
reading.correct: He walked in ahead of everyone, clearly leading them
reading.explain: The text says Зверков вошел впереди всех, видимо, предводительствуя — Zverkov entered in front of everyone, evidently leading them.

reading.ru: «Я с удивлением узнал о вашем желании участвовать с нами», — начал он, сюсюкивая и пришептывая, и растягивая слова, чего прежде с ним не бывало.
reading.question: How did Zverkov speak to the narrator, in a way unlike before?
options: Lisping and drawling his words affectedly
reading.correct: Lisping and drawling his words affectedly
reading.explain: The text says он ... сюсюкивая и пришептывая, и растягивая слова — he lisped, mumbled, and drawled his words, which he had never done before.

reading.ru: «Давно ждете?» — спросил Трудолюбов.
reading.question: What did Trudolyubov ask the narrator?
options: Whether he had been waiting long
reading.correct: Whether he had been waiting long
reading.explain: Trudolyubov asks «Давно ждете?» — "Have you been waiting long?"

reading.ru: «Я приехал ровно в пять часов, как мне вчера назначено», — отвечал я громко и с раздражением, обещавшим близкий взрыв.
reading.question: How did the narrator answer Trudolyubov's question about waiting?
options: Loudly and with irritation, noting he arrived exactly at five as arranged
reading.correct: Loudly and with irritation, noting he arrived exactly at five as arranged
reading.explain: He answered громко и с раздражением, saying he had arrived ровно в пять часов, as he had been told the day before.

reading.ru: «Это вовсе не смешно!» — закричал я Ферфичкину, раздражаясь все более и более.
reading.question: What did the narrator shout at Ferfichkin, growing more irritated?
options: That it was not funny at all
reading.correct: That it was not funny at all
reading.explain: The narrator shouts «Это вовсе не смешно!» — "This is not funny at all!" — at Ferfichkin.

reading.ru: «Садимся, господа», — закричал вошедший Симонов.
reading.question: What did Simonov call out as he entered?
reading.correct: "Let's sit down, gentlemen"
reading.explain: Simonov calls out «Садимся, господа» — "Let's sit down, gentlemen."

reading.ru: Стол был круглый.
reading.question: What shape was the dinner table?
reading.correct: Round
reading.explain: The text states plainly Стол был круглый — the table was round.

reading.ru: «Ну, а как ваше содержание?»
reading.question: What personal, somewhat prying question is the narrator asked at the table?
reading.correct: "Well, how is your income/salary?"
reading.explain: He is asked «Ну, а как ваше содержание?» — meaning his salary/allowance, which he finds embarrassing.

reading.ru: «Не богато», — важно заметил Зверков.
reading.question: What did Zverkov remark gravely after hearing the narrator's salary?
reading.correct: "Not very rich"
reading.explain: Zverkov remarks важно, «Не богато» — "Not very rich," belittling the sum.

reading.ru: я обедаю здесь, в кафе-ресторане, на свои деньги, не на свои, а не на чужие.
reading.question: What does the narrator insist about how he is paying for dinner?
options: That he is dining on his own money, not someone else's
That Simonov is paying for him
reading.correct: That he is dining on his own money, not someone else's
reading.explain: He insists, flustered, я обедаю здесь ... на свои деньги, не на свои, а не на чужие — on his own money, not someone else's.

reading.ru: А вот я вам лучше расскажу, как я третьего дня чуть не женился!
reading.question: What story does Zverkov offer to tell instead of continuing the argument?
options: How he almost got married two days before
How he traveled to the Caucasus
reading.correct: How he almost got married two days before
reading.explain: Zverkov says he will tell them как я третьего дня чуть не женился — how he nearly got married a couple of days ago.

reading.ru: Я пил с горя лафит и херес стаканами.
reading.question: What did the narrator do out of grief/frustration?
options: Drink claret and sherry by the glassful
reading.correct: Drink claret and sherry by the glassful
reading.explain: The text says Я пил с горя лафит и херес стаканами — he drank claret and sherry by the glassful out of grief.

reading.ru: Зверков рассказывал о какой-то пышной даме, которую он довел таки наконец до признания.
reading.question: What was Zverkov boasting about to the others?
options: A grand lady he had finally brought to a confession (of love)
A business deal he had closed
reading.correct: A grand lady he had finally brought to a confession (of love)
reading.explain: Zverkov tells of a пышная дама, которую он довел ... до признания — a grand lady he had finally brought to confess her feelings.

reading.ru: «Твое здоровье и счастливого пути!» — крикнул он Зверков.
reading.question: What toast is shouted to Zverkov?
reading.correct: "Your health and a good journey!"
reading.explain: Someone shouts «Твое здоровье и счастливого пути!» in Zverkov's honor, since the dinner is a farewell for his trip.

reading.ru: Зверков разлегся на кушетке, положив одну ногу на округлый столик.
reading.question: How did Zverkov position himself after they moved to the couch?
options: He sprawled on the couch, resting one leg on a round table
He sat stiffly upright in a chair
reading.correct: He sprawled on the couch, resting one leg on a round table
reading.explain: The text says Зверков разлегся на кушетке, положив одну ногу на округлый столик — he sprawled on the couch with one leg propped on a round little table.

reading.ru: Наконец дошло до того, что Шекспир бессмертен.
reading.question: What grand topic did the group's drunken conversation eventually reach?
reading.correct: That Shakespeare is immortal
reading.explain: The text notes their talk дошло до того, что Шекспир бессмертен — it got to the point of declaring Shakespeare immortal.

reading.ru: Я имел терпение проходить так прямо перед ними с восьми до одиннадцати часов.
reading.question: What did the narrator do obsessively for three hours, ignored by the others?
options: Pace back and forth in front of them from eight to eleven o'clock
reading.correct: Pace back and forth in front of them from eight to eleven o'clock
reading.explain: He says Я имел терпение проходить так прямо перед ними с восьми до одиннадцати часов — he had the patience to pace before them from eight to eleven.

reading.ru: Пробило одиннадцать.
reading.question: What time did the clock strike as the evening drew toward its end?
reading.correct: Eleven o'clock
reading.explain: The text simply states Пробило одиннадцать — it struck eleven.

reading.ru: «Симонов, дайте мне шесть рублей!» — сказал я решительно и отчаянно.
reading.question: What does the narrator desperately demand from Simonov at the end?
reading.correct: Six rubles
reading.explain: He says decisively and desperately, «Симонов, дайте мне шесть рублей!» — "Simonov, give me six rubles!"
